subject: Linguistics
title: First Words
description: A quick win: understand First Words.

hook.text: Most babies say their first word around 12 months. By 18 months, they're learning 10 new words a day.

buildup.text: First words are typically nouns for familiar objects—'mama,' 'dog,' 'ball,' 'water.'

discovery.text: The vocabulary spurt around 18 months happens when children realize everything has a name.

twist.text: Children's early words aren't always adults' categories—'dog' might mean any four-legged animal.

climax.text: By age six, children know about 14,000 words—they've been learning nearly one word per waking hour.

punchline.text: Children are the fastest language learners on Earth.

quiz.question: What triggers the vocabulary spurt around 18 months?
